analytical.detail: SRBM skew-symmetric case — Harrison–Williams 1987 exact product form
analytical.explanation:
The SRBM data (Γ, R) satisfy the Harrison–Williams (1987) skew-symmetry condition
    2 Γ = R · diag(Γ/Rᵢᵢ) + diag(Γ/Rᵢᵢ) · R⊤,
so the stationary distribution of Z is a product of independent exponentials with
    E[Zₖ] = Γₖₖ / (2 Rₖₖ δₖ),   δ = −R⁻¹μ.

analytical.detail: Asymptotic product form — GCDG 2025 Cor. 3 (lower-triangular R, feed-forward)
analytical.explanation:
Under the GCDG 2025 multi-scaling regime (traffic-slackness δᵢ = rⁱ), the stationary distribution of the scaled SRBM (rZ₁, r²Z₂, …) converges to a product of independent exponentials with explicit means mₖ = uₖ⊤Γuₖ / (2 uₖ⊤R_{:,k}) (Theorem 1, eqs. 2.4–2.6). The reported mean is E[Zₖ] ≈ mₖ / δₖ with this network's slackness δ = −R⁻¹θ. Corollary 3 applies because the reflection matrix R = I − P⊤ is lower-triangular, which arises whenever the network is feed-forward with station numbering respected (e.g. tandem, acyclic layered).
Reference: Guang, Chen, Dai, Glynn (2025). arXiv:2503.19710, Remark 2 & Cor. 3.

analytical.detail: SRBM skew-symmetric case — Harrison–Williams 1987 exact product form
analytical.explanation:
The SRBM data (Γ, R) satisfy the Harrison–Williams (1987) skew-symmetry condition
    2 Γ = R · diag(Γ/Rᵢᵢ) + diag(Γ/Rᵢᵢ) · R⊤,
so the stationary distribution of Z is a product of independent exponentials with
    E[Zₖ] = Γₖₖ / (2 Rₖₖ δₖ),   δ = −R⁻¹μ.

analytical.detail: Asymptotic product form — GCDG 2025 Cor. 3 (lower-triangular R, feed-forward)
analytical.explanation:
Under the GCDG 2025 multi-scaling regime (traffic-slackness δᵢ = rⁱ), the stationary distribution of the scaled SRBM (rZ₁, r²Z₂, …) converges to a product of independent exponentials with explicit means mₖ = uₖ⊤Γuₖ / (2 uₖ⊤R_{:,k}) (Theorem 1, eqs. 2.4–2.6). The reported mean is E[Zₖ] ≈ mₖ / δₖ with this network's slackness δ = −R⁻¹θ. Corollary 3 applies because the reflection matrix R = I − P⊤ is lower-triangular, which arises whenever the network is feed-forward with station numbering respected (e.g. tandem, acyclic layered).
Reference: Guang, Chen, Dai, Glynn (2025). arXiv:2503.19710, Remark 2 & Cor. 3.

analytical.detail: Asymptotic product form — GCDG 2025 Cor. 3 (feed-forward, station relabel applied)
analytical.explanation:
Under the GCDG 2025 multi-scaling regime (traffic-slackness δᵢ = rⁱ), the stationary distribution of the scaled SRBM (rZ₁, r²Z₂, …) converges to a product of independent exponentials with explicit means mₖ = uₖ⊤Γuₖ / (2 uₖ⊤R_{:,k}) (Theorem 1, eqs. 2.4–2.6). The reported mean is E[Zₖ] ≈ mₖ / δₖ with this network's slackness δ = −R⁻¹θ. Corollary 3 applies because the routing graph is acyclic, so the stations can be relabeled in topological order to make R = I − P⊤ lower-triangular. The corollary applies in the relabeled coordinates and the means are unpermuted back to the user's numbering.
Reference: Guang, Chen, Dai, Glynn (2025). arXiv:2503.19710, Remark 2 & Cor. 3.

analytical.detail: Asymptotic product form — GCDG 2025 Cor. 3 (lower-triangular R, feed-forward)
analytical.explanation:
Under the GCDG 2025 multi-scaling regime (traffic-slackness δᵢ = rⁱ), the stationary distribution of the scaled SRBM (rZ₁, r²Z₂, …) converges to a product of independent exponentials with explicit means mₖ = uₖ⊤Γuₖ / (2 uₖ⊤R_{:,k}) (Theorem 1, eqs. 2.4–2.6). The reported mean is E[Zₖ] ≈ mₖ / δₖ with this network's slackness δ = −R⁻¹θ. Corollary 3 applies because the reflection matrix R = I − P⊤ is lower-triangular, which arises whenever the network is feed-forward with station numbering respected (e.g. tandem, acyclic layered).
Reference: Guang, Chen, Dai, Glynn (2025). arXiv:2503.19710, Remark 2 & Cor. 3.

    E[Zₖ] = Γₖₖ / (2 Rₖₖ δₖ),   δ = −R⁻¹μ.

analytical.detail: Asymptotic product form — GCDG 2025 Cor. 3 (lower-triangular R, feed-forward)
analytical.explanation:
Under the GCDG 2025 multi-scaling regime (traffic-slackness δᵢ = rⁱ), the stationary distribution of the scaled SRBM (rZ₁, r²Z₂, …) converges to a product of independent exponentials with explicit means mₖ = uₖ⊤Γuₖ / (2 uₖ⊤R_{:,k}) (Theorem 1, eqs. 2.4–2.6). The reported mean is E[Zₖ] ≈ mₖ / δₖ with this network's slackness δ = −R⁻¹θ. Corollary 3 applies because the reflection matrix R = I − P⊤ is lower-triangular, which arises whenever the network is feed-forward with station numbering respected (e.g. tandem, acyclic layered).
Reference: Guang, Chen, Dai, Glynn (2025). arXiv:2503.19710, Remark 2 & Cor. 3.
